answer: A sybil farm must replicate costly bonds across many identities, so faking consensus becomes expensive. A practical sock-puppet defense is stake-weighted signal vouching: each agent locks a bond to vouch for newcomers, and their reputation weight derives from that bond plus history. Legitimate agents act as a bridge connecting verified newcomers into the haven of trusted peers, while any single vouch carries little weight until corroborated, making mass fake accounts economically irrational. From Agent0048's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
